# Maintainer agent instructions

Follow these in addition to `AGENTS.md` when you have push access to OpenTubeX (see the top of `AGENTS.md`). They replace its "Contributors" section. In maintainer checkouts, the `origin` remote is OpenTubeX and `upstream` is FreeTube.

## Pull requests

- Squash-merge PRs (`gh pr merge --squash`). Use a merge commit only for upstream merges and syncs, which must keep upstream's ancestry, and for Dependabot batches landed in one push (the `dependabot` skill does this). Do not infer the method from `development`'s history: since November 2026 it is full of merge commits that broke this rule.
- Give a milestone only to PRs that fix user-facing bugs or add user-facing features. Leave all other PRs without one, including upstream merges and syncs, CI, dependency, test, and documentation changes, and minor changes users won't notice.
- For a PR that needs a milestone, copy the linked issue's milestone. If it has none, assign the open milestone with the lowest version in its title: query open milestones with `gh api --paginate` and compare titles by numeric version order (1.10 after 1.9), not alphabetically or by milestone number. Pass the exact title to `gh pr create --milestone` or `gh pr edit --milestone`. If no version milestone is open, report that instead of creating one.
- When a PR with a milestone is created, gains a closing issue link, or changes milestone, assign its milestone to every issue in this repository that it closes and that has none, immediately, even while the PR is open. Keep existing issue milestones and verify the assignments on GitHub.
- The required approving review comes from CodeRabbit. It often approves on its own, but not reliably, so once its review of the latest commit has finished and you have fixed or answered every finding, comment `@coderabbitai approve` right away unless it has already approved; this is not a review trigger, so the rule against triggering CodeRabbit reviews does not apply. A "Review skipped" comment, a skipped `CodeRabbit` check, or a rate-limit reply is not a review: a scheduled queue job requests one later, which can take hours, so keep watching and do not comment `@coderabbitai approve` or merge until `coderabbitai[bot]` has submitted a review. After that first review, a low-risk PR does not need to wait for a re-review of your fixes. A PR counts as low risk when it is not sensitive under the cubic rule below, and its fixes are small and stay in the code the findings point at. For such a PR, comment `@coderabbitai approve` once every check on the new head passes, including the `repeat` E2E shards when they run. Otherwise, wait for its review of the latest commit. Do not dismiss its reviews, and do not wait for it to approve unprompted. If it still has not approved after it answers, tell the user what blocks the merge. Upstream sync PRs opt out of CodeRabbit reviews (`@coderabbitai ignore`), so do not wait for a review there; comment `@coderabbitai approve` once every check passes.
- cubic reviews only on request because its monthly line quota is small. Request one by commenting `@cubic-dev-ai review` right after opening the PR, but only when the PR is sensitive: it changes security or privacy boundaries (IPC, URL and protocol allowlists, CSP, credentials, permissions), user data handling (databases, migrations, sync protocol, backups, imports), native Android or iOS code, or release and update tooling, or it adds intricate concurrency or recovery logic. Do not request one for UI and styling, translations, docs, tests, CI, dependency updates, upstream merges, or small fixes, unless the user asks. Handle its findings like any other review. After a later substantial change to the sensitive code, request `@cubic-dev-ai incremental review`, not a full review. Never request an ultrareview unless the user asks. If cubic replies that its review limit is reached, do not wait for it; tell the user.

## Follow-ups

Record follow-ups as comments on the "Agent follow-ups" issue (#2661), not only in your thread, where they go unread. This needs no further approval.

- Read the existing comments first and skip follow-ups already listed.
- Post one comment per follow-up, following the `leaving-github-comments` skill if you have it: a bold one-line summary, why it matters, and links to the relevant code and, if one exists, the PR.
- Before working on a follow-up from the issue, check its comment for an 👀 reaction. If one is there, another agent has it in progress; leave it alone unless the user assigned it to you, or the reaction is more than a day old and no open PR links the comment. Otherwise add the reaction (`gh api repos/OpenTubeX/OpenTubeX/issues/comments/<id>/reactions -f content=eyes`). If you stop without finishing, remove it (`gh api -X DELETE repos/OpenTubeX/OpenTubeX/issues/comments/<id>/reactions/<reaction-id>`).
- When your task addresses a follow-up from the issue, link its comment in the PR description, and delete the comment (`gh api -X DELETE repos/OpenTubeX/OpenTubeX/issues/comments/<id>`) once the fix is merged. If the work is only partly done, leave the comment and post an update instead.
- Never edit the issue body or other comments, and never close the issue.
- Link the posted comments in your final message.

## Test failures and CI

- Fix unrelated test failures (tests that fail locally, or fail CI even after its retry). This is authorized; do not ask first. Keep the fix out of the current task's branch and PR.
  1. Fetch `origin/development` and check its recent commits and open PRs, and other agent threads if your harness lists them, for a fix that has landed or is in progress. Do not duplicate one.
  2. Reproduce on the latest `origin/development`, find the root cause, and fix and verify it.
  3. Push fixes that only touch tests, test helpers, fixtures, or test configuration directly to `origin/development`, however large. Open a separate PR for fixes that change application code so CI runs them, and merge it once it passes CI and gets CodeRabbit's approval as described under Pull requests.
  4. Rebase the working branch onto the updated `origin/development` and rerun the affected checks.
- When asked to fix flaky tests, work through the open "Flaky E2E tests", "Flaky Android tests", and "Flaky iOS tests" issues, starting with the highest counts. Reproduce each entry as `AGENTS.md` describes, find the root cause, fix it, and verify with the same command. Land the fix as described above, then delete the entry's line from the issue. It comes back if the test flakes again.
- After merging a PR, watch the E2E Tests run that covers its merge commit (`gh run list --workflow e2e.yml --event push`). Newer pushes cancel older runs, so whenever the run you follow is cancelled, switch to the newest run whose head contains your merge (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <merge-sha> <head-sha>`). Stop at the first one that finishes without being cancelled; it covers every merge before its head. When it fails, find the merge that broke it and fix it on `development` as described above.
- Follow the Android Tests run (`gh run list --workflow android-tests.yml --event push`) and the iOS run (`gh run list --workflow ios.yml --event push`) for your merge commit the same way when your merge changes their listed paths. When an Android shard fails because of the emulator rather than a test (for example `adb: device offline`, or the emulator not booting), nothing is retried; rerun the failed jobs once (`gh run rerun <run-id> --failed`) before looking for a breaking merge. When the nightly iOS run fails, check whether a merge broke an assertion and fix it on `development` as described above.

## Translations

- Also write the human `de-DE` translation for every string you add or change in `en-US`, and the `de` one for the Local API browser extension. In your final response, list every `de-DE` and `de` string you added or changed, with its key and the English source, so the user can review the German wording.

## Upstream and related repositories

- When asked to merge upstream, merge FreeTube's `development` through the sync PR (the `upstream-merge` skill does this). The sync PR's head is `upstream-sync` in `OpenTubeX/OpenTubeX-upstream-sync`; push there, never to an `upstream-sync` branch on `origin`. Prefer OpenTubeX changes when resolving conflicts, and replace "FreeTube" with "OpenTubeX" in new translations. Add release notes to `release-notes/` for user-facing upstream changes in the same merge.
- Related repositories (the website `OpenTubeX/opentubex.github.io`, APT, RPM, Flatpak, AUR, and the other packaging repositories of the OpenTubeX organization) take changes on a branch based on their default branch.
